summary:
We developed Draco Mission ([https://draco-mission.vercel.app/](https://draco-mission.vercel.app/)), an interactive web-based simulation game that places players in the role of aerospace engineers and mission directors. Participants design, manage, and simulate a complete space mission from scratch—selecting scientific objectives, configuring spacecraft subsystems and payloads, choosing launch vehicles and target orbits, and balancing real-time constraints including budget, mass, power, data capacity, and communications.

Our solution directly addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by bridging the gap between isolated theoretical concepts and real-world systems engineering. Instead of treating orbital mechanics, spacecraft design, and resource management separately, Draco Mission connects them into an interdependent ecosystem where every upgrade creates realistic engineering trade-offs.

This project is important because it democratizes space education. By turning complex aerospace constraints into an engaging, accessible, and hands-on game, Draco Mission fosters critical thinking and inspires students and future innovators to explore STEM careers.

Draco Mission: Space Mission Design Game

Integrantes:

Prof. Ariel Fernando Rodas ID: 29335044

Angelo Francisco Aguilera ID: 53899011

Salta - Argentina

1. What does it do or how does it work?

Draco Mission is an interactive simulation game designed to bring aerospace engineering and complex decision-making closer to students, enthusiasts, and future scientists. The game immerses participants in the role of space engineers and mission directors, challenging them to plan, design, and operate a complete space mission from scratch.

How does it work?

  • Objective Definition: The player starts by selecting a specific scientific or exploration goal for their mission.
  • Spacecraft & Payload Configuration: Users must choose scientific instruments, power systems, solar panels, batteries, communication systems, and the overall structure of the satellite or probe.
  • Orbit & Launch Selection: Players select a launch vehicle and a target orbit (such as Low Earth Orbit, Sun-Synchronous Orbit, etc.), ensuring that the spacecraft's mass does not exceed the rocket's payload capacity.
  • Real-Time Critical Resource Management: Throughout the simulation, the system evaluates physical and financial constraints live: Budget, Mass, Power (energy), Data Capacity, and Communications.
  • Simulation & Evaluation: The game processes the user's decisions and generates a performance report, indicating whether the mission succeeded, failed, or ran out of resources in space.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Experiential Learning (Learning by Playing): It transforms abstract theoretical concepts of physics and aerospace engineering (such as mass-to-power balance, launch windows, and orbital constraints) into an intuitive, hands-on experience.
  • Understanding Trade-offs: It visually and directly demonstrates that in real-world engineering, there is no single "perfect" solution; every upgrade in one category (e.g., a more powerful instrument) creates a cost or limitation in another (e.g., higher energy consumption and weight).
  • Educational Accessibility: It allows anyone, regardless of their prior technical background, to understand the real challenges faced by space agencies like NASA when designing deep-space missions or Earth-observation satellites.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • STEM Engagement: To inspire high school and university students to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics by showing that space exploration is a dynamic and accessible field.
  • Open Educational Tool: To serve as a supplementary pedagogical resource for physics, astronomy, and technology classrooms, helping educators explain complex systems through gamification.
  • Fostering Critical Thinking: To empower players to analyze multi-variable problems, manage budget constraints, and make decisions based on data and scientific logic.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Frontend Web Development & Logic: Built using modern web technologies (such as JavaScript/TypeScript and interactive UI frameworks) to ensure a smooth, cross-platform experience accessible directly from a web browser without heavy installations.
  • Deployment & Hosting Platform: Deployed on Vercel ([https://draco-mission.vercel.app/](https://draco-mission.vercel.app/)), enabling fast, secure, and global access for any user with an internet connection.
  • Design & Collaboration Tools: Version control environments (Git/GitHub) for teamwork, UI design tools, and NASA open resources (mission guides and conceptual space engineering models) to ensure the scientific accuracy of the game's variables.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Holistic Systemic Approach: Unlike other tools that isolate concepts (such as only calculating orbits or only launching a rocket), Draco Mission connects all variables of a space mission into an interdependent ecosystem where every decision directly impacts overall success.
  • Dynamic & Gamified Interface: It blends intuitive dashboard-style controls with the excitement of mission simulation, balancing engineering rigor with an engaging, modern, and playful experience.
  • Engineering Narrative: It turns constraint mathematics and physics into a narrative of survival and optimization, allowing the player to experience the real pressure of a mission control team.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Balance Between Fun and Scientific Rigor: The team ensured that the underlying math and physics (such as power consumption based on instrument load and mass-to-propulsion ratios) were scientifically coherent, yet presented in a friendly way to avoid overwhelming the player.
  • User Experience (UX/UI): A clean, responsive, and easy-to-navigate interface was prioritized, ensuring that resource counters (budget, mass, energy) remained visible at all times to provide immediate feedback on the user's choices.
  • Scalability & Accessibility: As a cloud-hosted web application (draco-mission.vercel.app), we considered it essential that it run seamlessly across computers and mobile devices with varying hardware capabilities.
